subject: Urgent: Traffic squeeze observed for Acme Analytics — immediate mitigation and playbook
messages:
From: Jordan Price <support@acme-analytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben.keller@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 429 spike + latency — Acme production (sample ids attached)

Vanessa / Marissa,

We started seeing an unusual spike in 429s and 500-level errors at ~08:50 PT this morning. Latency for our standard inference path (seq len ~1k) jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms over a 10-minute window and several of our busiest endpoints returned 429s for sustained periods.

Attached are a small sample of request IDs and agent-level traces (acme_request_samples.txt) — you'll see repeated 429s with a matching "quota exceeded" marker on the token bucket. We did not change anything on our side. This is causing user-facing failures for live features. Our primary contact: Ben Keller (ben.keller@acme-analytics.com).

Can your team confirm whether this is a capacity/backpressure event, or a policy misconfiguration (burst window/guardrail)? We need an ETA for mitigation and any temporary workarounds.

Thanks,
Jordan Price
Support Ops | Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_request_samples.txt (text/vnd.log)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Keller <ben.keller@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Sudden 429 spike + latency — Acme production (sample ids attached)

Team,

Forwarding an urgent escalation from Acme (external). Summary: rapid latency spike + 429s, customer reports token-bucket "quota exceeded" flags in traces. They claim no client-side change.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik / runtime: check the customer's effective quota, burst window, and any recent policy rollouts that touch the QPS gating and burst safety valve in us-west-2.
- Vivek / capacity: confirm current Dedicated pool headroom and whether any autoscale/backfill events occurred at 08:40-09:00 PT.
- Marissa: advise on communications and credit/SLA remediation if this is our misconfig.

I've uploaded their sample to Drive and attached a short incident summary (acme_incident_summary.pdf). Please reply with findings and next steps — Acme is on an enterprise contract; they want a 1-hour mitigation ETA.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_incident_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Sudden 429 spike + latency — Acme production (sample ids attached)

Vanessa — quick update from runtime: I've checked the policy graph and customer effective plan. Findings: 
- Acme was on a standard committed QPS plan but was recently moved to the new unified guardrail routing (rolled out last night). Their per-client burst window defaulted to 10s with an inadvertent global cap of 250 tokens due to a templating bug when inheriting the "safety-valve" profile.
- At ~08:46 PT we see their sustained short bursts triggered the safety valve which aggressively enforced a per-window drain; KV cache hit rates dropped temporarily (cache evictions observed) increasing latency.
- No capacity autoscale event logged in Dedicated pool for their tenant at that time — so this is policy-induced suppression, not raw GPU exhaustion.

Immediate mitigation I recommend (fast path):
1) Temporarily increase Acme's burst window cap from 250 -> 1500 tokens for 1 hour (proposed payload attached: proposed_quota_temporary_bump.json).
2) Roll back the last template change for the "safety-valve" inheritance for accounts with active commit (we should avoid blanket global caps).
3) Enable a short-lived per-account emergency bypass (rate-limit-exempt) for 5 minutes while we validate stability, then ramp down via a canary.

I'll run the increase now if you approve; it is a single API call to the policy manager (no infra deploy). We should also open an incident in OPS-9221 and prepare a customer note explaining root cause and remediation steps.

On Wed, Oct 30, 2029 at 09:12 AM Jordan Price <support@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Vanessa / Marissa,
>
> We started seeing an unusual spike in 429s and 500-level errors at ~08:50 PT this morning...

— Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Jordan Price <support@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Keller <ben.keller@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429 spike + latency — Acme production (sample ids attached)

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks for flagging. Quick summary and actions we've taken so you have a single source of truth: 
- Root cause: a policy rollout last night introduced a templating bug that applied an overly aggressive burst cap to some committed accounts; that cap suppressed bursts and caused those requests to fall back to slower paths, increasing latency and producing 429s.
- Immediate mitigations executed (09:55 PT): temporary burst cap increase for Acme -> 1500 tokens (1 hour), emergency bypass for 5 minutes while we validated, and rollback of the safety-valve inheritance template for committed accounts.
- Current status (12:00 PT): request rates and error rates back to baseline; latency normalized to ~140ms for Acme test trace. No Dedicated capacity changes required.

Next steps / asks:
1) Karthik / Runtime to produce a short postmortem and a patch to the templating logic (target: EOD tomorrow).
2) Marissa / AMs to propose customer remediation (one month of usage credit + SLA remediation for affected window) — please advise if exec sign-off is required.
3) Ops to add a canary for future guardrail rollouts and automated verification against per-account commit plans.

We'll schedule a 30-min readout with Acme at 15:00 PT today to walk through the timeline and next steps. If you want me to loop in Legal or Sales Leadership, say the word — Marissa, any preference?

Appreciate the rapid responses.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_post_actions.txt (text/plain)
